free_tier.stated: A free localhost tunnel with a stable HTTPS URL. No signup, no client install. Stable URLs are tied to your SSH key; the server is open source (MIT).

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel or an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: No byte allowance. Limits are per request and per connection: 128 MB per request and response body, 1 GB per direction per WebSocket connection, 3 tunnels per IP.; ingress: http-only

chaining: A zero-install webhook or demo endpoint; no path to UDP.

limits.value: 50 requests/s per tunnel, 25/s per visitor IP, 10 new SSH connections per minute per IP
128 MB request and response body; 1 GB per direction per WebSocket
about 2.37 MiB (2,486,272 bytes) per request on the free anonymous tier

binding_note: 1 TiB/month is 3.24 Mbit/s sustained, which the byte path could carry, but the 50 requests/s per tunnel and 128 MB body caps define what the service is for. Only port 80 is forwarded, so a UDP datagram has no path at all.

identity_cost.detail: Any SSH key works; there is no account, sign-up or key registration. The subdomain is derived from the public key with HMAC-SHA256.

reliability_note: TLS terminates at the edge, so it is not end-to-end encrypted; a phishing interstitial appears for first-time visitors; the server is MIT and self-hostable. A harness measured a 908 ms median latency and both 4 MiB transfers stopping at exactly 2,486,272 bytes, a per-request cap of about 2.37 MiB on the free anonymous tier.
confidence_note: A measured run would show the real throughput ceiling; the protocol limitation is already decisive for UDP. the anonymous tier caps a request at about 2.37 MiB and measures a 908 ms median latency (measured 2026-11-05).

evidence.proved: SSH reverse tunnel on port 80 with a stable HTTPS URL per SSH key; limits table with 3 tunnels per IP, 50 requests/s per tunnel, 128 MB bodies, 1 GB per WebSocket direction.
Launch date and pitch: stable localhost URLs over SSH with no installs, free to use, open-source MIT server.
both 4 MiB transfers stopped at exactly 2,486,272 bytes on the free anonymous tier

notes: SSH-based reverse tunneling service. Provides stable public hostnames derived from client SSH keys without requiring account registration.

extras.wg_detail: Only port 80 is forwarded over SSH and served as HTTPS: ssh -t -R 80:localhost:3000 proxy.tunnl.gg. There is no UDP or raw TCP listener.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance. Limits are per request and per connection: 128 MB per request and response body, 1 GB per direction per WebSocket connection, 3 tunnels per IP.
extras.transit_note: The tunnl.gg edge terminates TLS and forwards down the SSH connection.
